Fresh gfx1100-rdna3-final-inventory-20260929 identifies ELF fnv1a64:8bb55d99e9033567. The target-native ConSan oracle in hip-moi 028_gfx1100_wmma_streamk_arrival_counter_test.hip lines 241-283 stores each of two waves' WMMA partials to LDS, then lane zero executes the selected agent-scope global_atomic_add_u32. The wave observing old value 1 consumes both waves' partials. Inventory places the atomic at .text+0x015c, immediately after the LDS completion wait at 0x0154 and release s_waitcnt_vscnt at 0x0158; the acquire cache pair remains at 0x0168/0x0170. Weaken only the release edge. The maintained ConSanOracleAcqRelFetchAddOrdersWmmaPartials command launches both waves and verifies the complete output. Eight independent trials per profile and a minimum of six detections are predeclared before outcomes.

Fresh gfx1100-rdna3-final-inventory-20260929 identifies ELF fnv1a64:151f1a1b92c384b1. The target-native ConSan oracle in hip-moi 029_gfx1100_wmma_streamk_tree_atomic_or_test.hip lines 279-329 stores four waves' WMMA partials to LDS. Lane zero of each of the first three waves publishes its bit with the selected release global_atomic_or_b32 at .text+0x03c0 after the LDS wait at 0x03b8 and release s_waitcnt_vscnt at 0x03bc. The fourth wave polls for all producer bits, then executes the distinct returning acquire/release OR at 0x01e0 and consumes every wave's partials. Select occurrence 1 to weaken only the producer release boundary while preserving the consumer acquire sequence. The maintained ConSanOracleAcqRelBitmaskOrdersWmmaPartials command cannot complete its numerical check without all producer publications. Eight independent trials per profile and a minimum of six detections are predeclared before outcomes.

The reviewed gfx1100 kernel selected by this fault dispatches one 128-thread workgroup (four wave32 waves) with 16 KiB LDS for RocblasGemmTest.Square_64x64, M=N=K=64, alpha=1, beta=0. The first publication block is bypassed only when K>>4 is zero; K=64 makes that condition false, so the selected initial-publication s_barrier is reached unconditionally for this command. LDS producer stores are followed by two LDS completion waits, the singleton s_barrier, and ds_load_b128 consumers. Producer addresses are 16*thread_id; consumer addresses are 16*(thread_id%16), so peer waves consume data produced by lanes 0..15 of wave 0. Removing this barrier exposes cross-wave publication while preserving the waits. The exact site selector binds this proof to the reviewed code object; rediscover and review the site if its identity changes. Select the singleton barrier by exact site, without a paired-sequence selector. Calibration policy: evaluate Default presets default/high/higher/max in ascending order and stop at the first operating point with at least 6/8 admitted and reached detections; SuperCollider uses sleep=15 with the same threshold. Every operating point requires its own clean comparator. Timeout, bad output alone, trap, or signal does not count as detection.
